abstract: Neurons could offset the conductance load imposed by their dendrites through channel expression (compensation), or channel expression could move with that load (reinforcement); which arrangement holds in adult cortex is unknown. Writing rheobase as the product of input conductance and an effective-voltage factor turns the question into a sign test. In mouse cortical GABAergic Patch-seq neurons, after removal of transcriptomic type and covariates, an out-of-fold channel-gene score co-varies positively with residual input conductance (median Spearman {rho} = 0.32 over 20 cross-fitting splits, n = 493) and with a conductance score predicted from dendritic morphology alone ({rho} = 0.23, n = 483). The association is carried mainly by Sst and Pvalb cells and is close to zero in Vip cells. Its slope on the compensation axis is 0.13, against -1 for compensation and 0 for independence, so the finding concerns direction rather than magnitude: it excludes a population-wide compensation rule without implying strong amplification. Reduced NEURON models show that a compensatory correction is biophysically feasible, and the morphology-derived conductance predictor transfers from mouse to human reconstructions ({rho} = 0.27, n = 128).
